title: Arbora
code_edition: Québec Construction Code (edition unstated in case study); RBQ's 2015 guide for mass-timber buildings up to 12 storeys is discussed
document_date: Unknown; PDF publication date not stated

facts.text: The case study describes Arbora as an eight-storey project and says the Québec Construction Code required 2-hour fire resistance for load-bearing elements and 1- or 2-hour separations depending on location.
It says test results from the Origine project informed equivalent measures provided to the RBQ and the subsequent RBQ guide.
It describes a fire-load comparison with a similar noncombustible building as part of the rationale for leaving some glulam beams and columns exposed.

The Canadian Wood Council rehabilitation report describes an October 2018 balcony fire on the third storey and reports limited interior damage after a broken window; it describes the building's fire-safety features as limiting further spread.
facts.locator: Rehabilitation of Mass Timber Following Fire and Sprinkler Activation, PDF p.29 (printed p.25)

limitations: The case-study code edition is unstated.
No Arbora-specific alternative-solution application, fire-load calculation, full test reports or RBQ decision were located.
The incident report is an outcome reference, not evidence that another design is acceptable.
